references.text: The priest shall sprinkle blood on the altar seven times to cleanse it and consecrate it from the impurity of the Israelites, which expands on the cleansing process described in verse 16.
Refers to sins committed unintentionally among the children of Israel, which are part of the sins from which the sanctuary must be cleansed.
God promises to dwell among the Israelites, explaining why the sanctuary must be cleansed—because God dwells among them amidst their impurity.
The Lord will dwell among the children of Israel, emphasizing the necessity of cleansing the tent of meeting where God lives among His people.
Unclean persons must be sent out of the camp so as not to defile the camp where the Lord dwells among them.
The land must not become unclean, for the Lord dwells among the children of Israel, reflecting the idea that the sanctuary must be cleansed.
The house of Israel has defiled God's holy name through their sins, yet God will still dwell among them forever.
The high priest enters the Most Holy Place once a year with blood for his own sins and for the unintentional sins of the people, directly referring to the Yom Kippur ritual.
Almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and the heavenly things had to be purified with better sacrifices than animal blood—the blood of Christ.
Christ entered the holy place once for all by His own blood and secured eternal redemption, fulfilling the ritual of the Day of Atonement.
